theme: The moment a client stops asking for a proposal and starts calling you first

linkedin.text:
A VP of HR told me something I keep coming back to:

"At some point I just stopped sending RFPs to three different vendors. I call you first now."

That sentence is the clearest measure of what we're actually building — not the headcount at a gala, not the destination on the agenda. The moment a client trusts you enough to skip the procurement dance.

It takes consistency. It takes someone picking up at 11 PM when the venue in Lisbon has a problem. It takes delivering the same quality whether the group is 40 people in Prague or 400 in Bangkok.

We've been doing this since 2010. 1,500+ events. 130+ destinations. 25,000+ participants.

If you're an HR, marketing, or sales leader thinking about your next conference or incentive program — I'd rather have a 20-minute conversation before you write the brief than respond to an RFP after. Happy to connect.

facebook.text:
Our client's VP of HR said something that stuck with us:

"I stopped sending RFPs to three vendors. I just call you now."

That shift — from vendor to default partner — doesn't happen by accident. It happens after the third event lands exactly as promised, after the team in Singapore gets the same attention as the team in Tel Aviv, after something goes sideways at 11 PM and someone picks up.

We've been building toward that kind of trust since 2010. 1,500+ events delivered. 130+ destinations. The number we're most proud of? The clients who've stopped counting proposals.

Running a conference, incentive trip, or product launch this year? Let's talk before the brief is written. Drop a comment or send us a message.
